entries.b0f5c7084139f6bd: TAIYO YUDEN CO., LTD. and 29 subsidiaries and 1 affiliate form the group. Roles are clearly divided: manufacturing companies are dedicated to production, processing raw materials and semi-finished products supplied by the parent and other related companies into finished products and supplying them within the group. Sales companies sell finished products in Japan and overseas, and manufacturing-sales companies may also process products and sell them directly to set makers. The number of employees is 20,604 (because the company has a single segment, no breakdown by business is disclosed). Manufacturing is centered in Gunma Prefecture, where the parent’s Haruna Plant, Tamamura Plant, Yawatabara Plant and R&D Center are all located; in addition, subsidiaries in Niigata, Fukushima and Wakayama, and subsidiaries in Malaysia, China, South Korea and the Philippines, are responsible for manufacturing.

entries.c0af8916f542307c: This business manufactures and sells electronic components such as capacitors, inductors and composite devices. This is the only business of the TAIYO YUDEN Group, and the securities report states: "Since the company has a single segment, the electronic components business, no description related to segment information is provided." TAIYO YUDEN CO., LTD. and manufacturing-related affiliates process products into finished goods, which are sold through sales-related affiliates to set manufacturers and others in Japan and overseas; the company also supplies raw materials and semi-finished products to manufacturing-related affiliates. Consolidated net sales for the fiscal year ended March 2026 were ¥355,341 million (up 4.1% year on year), and operating profit was ¥19,996 million (up 91.2%). The company attributes this to higher sales in automotive and information infrastructure and industrial equipment applications.
entries.c451844504c1ed25: Its main products are multilayer ceramic capacitors that store electrical charge, inductors that smooth electrical current, communication devices (FBAR/SAW) and circuit modules that filter radio waves, and aluminum electrolytic capacitors made by consolidated subsidiary ELNA CO., LTD. Production for the fiscal year ended March 2026 (calculated at average selling prices during the period) was capacitors ¥254,843 million, inductors ¥65,441 million, other ¥27,039 million and composite devices ¥12,481 million, for a total of ¥359,806 million, an increase of 6.4% from the previous year. The company explains that it develops from materials and, leveraging its strength in technological capability, creates high value-added, high-quality products.
entries.c8156ea74f644f38: Consolidated revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥355,341 million, an increase of 4.1% from the previous year. The company explains that this was mainly due to higher sales to the automotive and information infrastructure and industrial equipment fields. By product category, capacitors rose on higher sales to automotive and information infrastructure and industrial equipment customers to ¥251,771 million (up 8.5%); inductors rose mainly on higher sales to consumer and information equipment customers to ¥64,319 million (up 4.5%); composite devices fell as both communication devices and circuit modules declined, to ¥14,796 million (down 35.6%); and other fell as aluminum electrolytic capacitors declined, to ¥24,453 million (down 1.5%).

entries.f436f0122a08cdaa: Its products do not reach consumers on their own; they are used by being built into the equipment of set makers. Revenue by region for the fiscal year ended March 2026 (classified by customer location) was China ¥104,774 million, other countries or regions ¥84,310 million, Hong Kong ¥50,453 million, Taiwan ¥40,690 million, Europe ¥27,667 million, North America ¥26,971 million and Japan ¥20,474 million, so sales to Japan account for only a part of the total. As no specific customer accounts for 10% or more of revenue, customer names are omitted. The company positions automotive and information infrastructure and industrial equipment as markets to focus on, and states that under its “Medium-Term Management Plan 2030” it aims to raise the sales ratio of these markets to 60%.
entries.fee927ef8b4a4a4e: Operating profit for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥19,996 million, an increase of 91.2% from the previous year. Together with non-operating income including foreign exchange gains of ¥4,759 million, ordinary profit was ¥24,129 million (up 129.4%), and net income attributable to owners of the parent was ¥14,806 million (up 535.9%), reflecting special losses including impairment losses of ¥2,130 million and business restructuring expenses of ¥1,455 million. The company continues to expand capacity to meet growing demand, and under its “Medium-Term Management Plan 2030” it plans capital expenditure on a scale of ¥270 billion over 5 years.
